[quote=lavinsworth_united_islands;60022531]Barely a day later, the meeting is set. At a small costal town nearly split in two by the border, a tiny cafe is surrounded by black SUVs and armored cars for the event, drawing considerable interest from the locals and tourists who are routinely ushered away after a bit of staring, however the news crews aren't deterred that easily. Inside, a very anxious waiter takes the order of the party of three.

"Could I get a water as well as two croissants please?" Mr. Achebe says, turning to his colleagues.
"Oh yes..." his advisor murmurs, shuffling around a few papers he was looking at from a grey folder. "I'll just get a coffee, and a generous amount of milk in that if you could." A second goes by before the local governor speaks up. "Same for me darling," she says before standing up and talking to one of the servicemen inside the cafe, murmuring something about the news. The man nods and walk outside and the governor sits down again, looking a bit calmer than before.

The cafe worker double checks their list and swiftly walks off to make the orders, leaving the three to talk in the few minutes that they have left till the foreign diplomats arrive. 

"Cozy place huh? You aught to know that an image of this visit is gonna be on the wall somewhere here." the governor say, watching each of the men for a good reaction. 

"It's a funny thing, seeing your image on the wall of someplace you have visited. I don't mind it though, I still have a signed movie poster from my teens, so I see it as somewhat the same thing." Mr. Achebe pauses for a second looking outside to observe if anything has happened with the news yet. "I much prefer this to stuffy meeting rooms and those big buildings we normally invite the international community to."

"Cheaper to finance too." Says the advisor, looking up at Mr. Achebe then back down at his papers. "They should be here soon. I give it 10 minutes or less."

[nation]Shahzada[/nation] RP[/quote]

President Fereydun Khan and Minister of Defence Arman Shari arrive in a military convoy to the town. The Dhora military was alerted to be at heightened readiness for the meeting. The Dhora convoy parks on a nearby street and the President and Minister leave their BTR-80.

"A small town for the meeting. It doesn't suit me. I would have preferred for a meeting out in the open. No chance of anything underhanded that way," President Khan says while walking at his usual brisk pace towards the cafe, paying the news crews no attention.

"Our men are ready should anything happen," Minister Shari says, slightly winded as he follows behind.

When they both make it to the cafe, they pat their concealed holsters and walk in. "There they are," whispers Minister Shari as he points towards the table where the Lavian delegation is seated. "Let's see what these Lavians want," President Khan whispers back.

President Khan takes a seat first before motioning for Minister Shari to do the same. "I would have preferred a meeting elsewhere but regardless, I want to know what has your country nervous about us, Representative Minister Achebe."

[b]- Battle of Al-Sharwa -[/b]

[spoiler=[b]Prelude[/b]]
With the capture of Aduab by THEP forces, Sal-Baliz was essentially out of urban centers - They no longer could reliably draft its population to fight in the holy war. This did not mean that Sal-Baliz was entirely undefended and syphoned of resources, many industrial centers remained intact, and dedicated all of their efforts to fuel the decaying Sal-Baliz war machine. Al-Sharwa was amongst these industrial centers, located south of Aduab. Al-Sharwa was a mostly flat desert, with occasional rocky hills and mountains dotting the landscape, and several veins of rivers cut through the south of the region - Al-Sharwa is also the origin point of prehistoric kingdoms of the area, featuring ziggurats and the like. The survivors of the fall of Aduab, including the supreme leader himself, rushed to meet their allies waiting in Al-Sharwa. Elevated regions, and vital zones were fortified and occupied by Sal-Baliz forces, who were determined to cause as much damage as possible to the invading Hydronians.

High command tasked the 3rd Turvek assault unit to secure the region, solidifying THEPs foothold in Aduab and cutting off vital industry from Sal-Baliz. The 2nd Yorgulun was busy in maintaining the occupation of Aduab, but the Hydronian command was confident in 3rd Turveks abilities to take the region. On 1st of August, the assault on Al-Sharwa had begun. 
[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Battle[/b]]
Hydronian High Command designated several vital points in Al-Sharwa. The urban settlement of Bazeyr, defended entirely by infantry, with several layers of trenchworks built facing west, where the Hydronians would come from. Helicopters and jets patrolled the skies, searching for Sal-Baliz armored columns and defenses. The 17th Armored Division advanced to assault Bazeyr, their ATGV-18Bs being the spearhead, followed by Otokars APCs. Infantry jumped into the trenches, clearing them out while the armor advanced. One by one, the layers fell, until Hydronia reached the town proper. Otokars took the lead, followed closely by infantry - A whack-the-mole type of conflict started, with Sal-Baliz forces trying to take out Otokars before they saw them, and vice-versa. Eventually, after only half an hour of combat, the town's police station fell to Hydronia, following the town's hall, resulting in the total capitulation of Bazeyr's defenders - Next on the list was the oil refinery and the oil fields, and before the Hydronians could even reach it, the two facilities were desperately demolished by Sal-Baliz. The oil lit up, and pyres of black smoke filled the horizon. Dismissing concerns from the soldiers, Hydronian High Command ordered their troops to engage the retreating Sal-Baliz. The smoke blocked the tank's normal view, and the fire turned certain spots practically impossible to be analyzed visually with thermal vision. Tank squadrons of the 17th, 16th and 13th Armored Divisions assumed overwatch positions around the fire, gunning down any Sal-Baliz force that left the smoke and fire, jets roamed the air, landing missiles into any armored column that they could find. Hydronian forces made one last sweep of the area by nightfall, and although the soldiers were already exhausted by this point, Military Command ordered the offensive to continue through the night. The Hydronian soldiers pushed themselves, taking more and more towns in the Al-Sharwa area, facing several ambushes amd layers of trenchworks. By morning, the Hydronians reached the ziggurats of Al-Sharwa.
Hydronian infantry, protected by the armor of Otokars, advanced to the sloped walls of the ancient temples, flushing into its courtyards, cleaning the surface before heading to secure the zigurrat's catacombs. Sal-Baliz placed artillery pieces, machine guns and anti-tank cannons on top of the walls, halting the advance of the tanks and Otokars until air support could come in and disable the guns. By mid-day, most of Al-Sharwa was secured, with the execption of a small pocket of Sal-Baliz armored squadrons down east - A extensive muddy marshland, created by the flooding of the several rivers in the region, stood between Hydronia and the Sal-Baliz. Almost all of the 3rd Turvek took part in the advance - The main battle tanks, followed by Otokars, trailed the most solid paths in the mud, under the cover of artillery and helicopters. Though some of the tanks eventually got stuck in the mud, the superior armor of the ATGV-18B allowed the tank to resist several shots from the older Sal-Baliz tanks - The Otokars had less luck, and several were destroyed before they could reach enemy lines. The surviving crews of the stuck vehicles were simply left behind to be rescued after the battle ended. Hydronian soldiers jumped from their vehicles when they reached the enemy trenches, fighting in intense close quarters combat, going trench by trench and bunker by bunker while the MBTs and the helicopters finished off what remained of the Sal-Baliz armor.

After searching the trenches through, the Hydronians came across a small bunker. Inside, Supreme leader Madhi Falah hidden behind a large ammo box. He opened fire on the troops, but they quickly surrounded him and shot him in the, making him immobile. The struggling leader would then be injected with an incapacitating agent and transported to a military camp, where he will be kept until THEP makes a further decision. 

By sunset, almost all enemy presence in Al-Sharwa was cleared out, and the battle was considered a great victory by Hydronian Command - Now, nothing can challenge the THEP rule over Sal-Baliz territory. The Hydronians have captured the east and the Bobians have the west. Throughout the next week, units will be deployed to capture smaller settlements and draw any remaining troops out of hiding.
[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Security Notice[/b]]
Over the coming days, it is likely that surviving Sal-Baliz soldiers and operatives will flee the territory to nearby nations or nations with connections to the Sal-Baliz. THEP has issued a security notice to several nearby governments warning them that Sal-Baliz members may be within their nation and advised them to arrest any Sal-Baliz members, then to either turn them over to THEP or to be tried for acts of terror and war crimes under the nations own justice system.

[u]Governments receiving a notice[/u]
[nation]Ferneus[/nation] (nearby nation with limited border control & law enforcement)
[nation]Dhornaper[/nation] (nearby nation with little stability after recent coup and militaristic government)
[nation]Al-Quzzam[/nation] (nearby nation under islamic governance)
[nation]Arkisiran[/nation] (nearby nation under Islamic governance)
[nation]Oceanice republic[/nation] (connections to the Sal-Baliz through Al-Qadi)
[nation]Baladullah[/nation] (nearby nation with high Islamic population)
[nation]Kaaganika[/nation] (nearby nation with limited stability due to recent civil war)
[nation]Nordiheim[/nation] (nearby nation with limited border control)

[i]*OOC: you dont have to RP that there are Sal-Baliz in your country, Im not tryna force anything on you :)*[/i]
[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Prelude[/b]]
With the capture of Aduab by THEP forces, Sal-Baliz was essentially out of urban centers - They no longer could reliably draft its population to fight in the holy war. This did not mean that Sal-Baliz was entirely undefended and syphoned of resources, many industrial centers remained intact, and dedicated all of their efforts to fuel the decaying Sal-Baliz war machine. Al-Sharwa was amongst these industrial centers, located south of Aduab. Al-Sharwa was a mostly flat desert, with occasional rocky hills and mountains dotting the landscape, and several veins of rivers cut through the south of the region - Al-Sharwa is also the origin point of prehistoric kingdoms of the area, featuring ziggurats and the like. The survivors of the fall of Aduab, including the supreme leader himself, rushed to meet their allies waiting in Al-Sharwa. Elevated regions, and vital zones were fortified and occupied by Sal-Baliz forces, who were determined to cause as much damage as possible to the invading Hydronians.

High command tasked the 3rd Turvek assault unit to secure the region, solidifying THEPs foothold in Aduab and cutting off vital industry from Sal-Baliz. The 2nd Yorgulun was busy in maintaining the occupation of Aduab, but the Hydronian command was confident in 3rd Turveks abilities to take the region. On 1st of August, the assault on Al-Sharwa had begun. 
[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Battle[/b]]
Hydronian High Command designated several vital points in Al-Sharwa. The urban settlement of Bazeyr, defended entirely by infantry, with several layers of trenchworks built facing west, where the Hydronians would come from. Helicopters and jets patrolled the skies, searching for Sal-Baliz armored columns and defenses. The 17th Armored Division advanced to assault Bazeyr, their ATGV-18Bs being the spearhead, followed by Otokars APCs. Infantry jumped into the trenches, clearing them out while the armor advanced. One by one, the layers fell, until Hydronia reached the town proper. Otokars took the lead, followed closely by infantry - A whack-the-mole type of conflict started, with Sal-Baliz forces trying to take out Otokars before they saw them, and vice-versa. Eventually, after only half an hour of combat, the town's police station fell to Hydronia, following the town's hall, resulting in the total capitulation of Bazeyr's defenders - Next on the list was the oil refinery and the oil fields, and before the Hydronians could even reach it, the two facilities were desperately demolished by Sal-Baliz. The oil lit up, and pyres of black smoke filled the horizon. Dismissing concerns from the soldiers, Hydronian High Command ordered their troops to engage the retreating Sal-Baliz. The smoke blocked the tank's normal view, and the fire turned certain spots practically impossible to be analyzed visually with thermal vision. Tank squadrons of the 17th, 16th and 13th Armored Divisions assumed overwatch positions around the fire, gunning down any Sal-Baliz force that left the smoke and fire, jets roamed the air, landing missiles into any armored column that they could find. Hydronian forces made one last sweep of the area by nightfall, and although the soldiers were already exhausted by this point, Military Command ordered the offensive to continue through the night. The Hydronian soldiers pushed themselves, taking more and more towns in the Al-Sharwa area, facing several ambushes amd layers of trenchworks. By morning, the Hydronians reached the ziggurats of Al-Sharwa.
Hydronian infantry, protected by the armor of Otokars, advanced to the sloped walls of the ancient temples, flushing into its courtyards, cleaning the surface before heading to secure the zigurrat's catacombs. Sal-Baliz placed artillery pieces, machine guns and anti-tank cannons on top of the walls, halting the advance of the tanks and Otokars until air support could come in and disable the guns. By mid-day, most of Al-Sharwa was secured, with the execption of a small pocket of Sal-Baliz armored squadrons down east - A extensive muddy marshland, created by the flooding of the several rivers in the region, stood between Hydronia and the Sal-Baliz. Almost all of the 3rd Turvek took part in the advance - The main battle tanks, followed by Otokars, trailed the most solid paths in the mud, under the cover of artillery and helicopters. Though some of the tanks eventually got stuck in the mud, the superior armor of the ATGV-18B allowed the tank to resist several shots from the older Sal-Baliz tanks - The Otokars had less luck, and several were destroyed before they could reach enemy lines. The surviving crews of the stuck vehicles were simply left behind to be rescued after the battle ended. Hydronian soldiers jumped from their vehicles when they reached the enemy trenches, fighting in intense close quarters combat, going trench by trench and bunker by bunker while the MBTs and the helicopters finished off what remained of the Sal-Baliz armor.

After searching the trenches through, the Hydronians came across a small bunker. Inside, Supreme leader Madhi Falah hidden behind a large ammo box. He opened fire on the troops, but they quickly surrounded him and shot him in the, making him immobile. The struggling leader would then be injected with an incapacitating agent and transported to a military camp, where he will be kept until THEP makes a further decision. 

By sunset, almost all enemy presence in Al-Sharwa was cleared out, and the battle was considered a great victory by Hydronian Command - Now, nothing can challenge the THEP rule over Sal-Baliz territory. The Hydronians have captured the east and the Bobians have the west. Throughout the next week, units will be deployed to capture smaller settlements and draw any remaining troops out of hiding.
